correctness.rationale: The seven nontrivial character quotients of the tame \((C_2)^3\)-cover have genera 2,2,2,2,2,2,5, producing 17 explicit independent regular differentials, equal to the genus by Riemann-Hurwitz. At the branch \(x=-1\), u is a local parameter; even and odd differential valuations reduce to normalized square roots of exact rational polynomial ratios. Full 11-by-14 and 6-by-8 matrices computed in \(\mathbb F_{11}[\alpha]/(\alpha^2+1)\) have pivot indices (0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,12,13) and (0,1,2,3,6,7), pivot minors 1 and 4, and full row ranks. All coefficients are embedded and regenerated by a standalone standard-library verifier. The resulting 17 gaps determine exactly \(\langle10,11,12,18,26\rangle\) with conductor 28. Published automorphisms act transitively on the 48 rational branch places; their base-value action is also checked exhaustively. No finite experiment is used to infer an unproved infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The initiating genus-17 curve paper calculates genus, maximality, automorphisms, and a particular Riemann-Roch dimension at \(18P\), but does not give the 17-term gap sequence, minimal generators, or conductor for the short orbit. The 2024 and 2026 semigroup papers address Hermitian subfields and maximal Fermat curves, whereas the initiating curve is explicitly not a Hermitian subfield. Searches for the precise curve, equations, gap sequence, semigroup generators, and broader multiquadratic-cover formulas revealed no explicit or dominating statement. An unindexed computation remains a residual originality risk.

value.rationale: The exact Weierstrass semigroup at the naturally distinguished 48-point branch orbit of the first known \(\mathbb F_{p^2}\)-maximal genus-17 non-Hermitian-subfield example is a complete intrinsic local arithmetic-geometric invariant. It upgrades the motivating paper's single dimension \(\(L(18P)\)\) check to all one-point Riemann-Roch dimensions, specifies multiplicity 10 and conductor 28, and provides concrete pole-order input for one-point algebraic-geometry codes. Computing the full sequence involves nontrivial cancellations among seven different character components rather than a degree/genus substitution; the exact answer was not implied by published prior results.
